purpose: Direct-access diagnosis, not a new production change or availability benchmark.
transport: Native Node HTTPS/HTTP2, no proxy agent, explicit edge lookup, normal certificate verification. Browser NetLog separately verified DIRECT and production secure DoH.

browserEvidence.observation: A/AAAA/HTTPS DoH streams received no headers/body before resolver HTTP/2 sessions failed with ERR_HTTP2_PING_FAILED (-352) at about 30 seconds. Navigation deadline was 20 seconds.
A/AAAA completed around 15.2 seconds; HTTPS lookup did not complete. TCP connected to configured address; no completed TLS handshake observed before navigation cancellation.
A response around 20.75 seconds; HTTPS headers around 22.03 seconds, no body in captured timeline. DNS already exceeded the 20-second page deadline.
TLS 1.3, accepted ECH and HTTP/2. Empty HTTP 403 with x-server: x-web and server: cloudflare envoy; no explicit cf-mitigated challenge header observed. Specific rejection policy unknown.
TLS 1.3, accepted ECH and HTTP/2. HTTP 403 with cf-mitigated: challenge and Just a moment page.

productionConfiguration.requiredInitialHttpsLookup: DNS_RULE_ENV_META_QUERY matches all original HTTPS query types, not just Meta domains, and requires resolver lookup before later synthesis.
productionConfiguration.interpretation: Additional serial dependency and optimization candidate; not established as the cause of pre-TLS or HTTP/2 ping failures. Removing it may change negative-response semantics.

conclusions: Upstream-free control requests also time out before TLS completion: at least part of the failure precedes HTTP request handling and cannot be caused by DNS cache eligibility or upstream lookup.
Both tested edges and both protocols have failures. Neither HTTP/2-only failure nor an edge-pinning fix is established.
A padded Facebook HTTPS query succeeds in 1431ms in one fixed-edge sample, so this query path is not permanently broken.
X and NodeSeek reach HTTP rejection/challenge after TLS and ECH; these are different from the DNS transport failures.
limitations: No packet capture or matching server-side durations. Cannot assign responsibility to ISP, Wi-Fi gateway, Cloudflare edge or another intermediary.

Observability event tool failed its response schema because a requestId was absent. Calculation results contained ACCESS_DENIED events that cannot be attributed to these authorized probes; successful invocation logging was disabled.
Initial 12 harness attempts failed before connection due to an incorrect custom Node lookup contract; excluded from network-failure counts. Original private records retained.
Single bounded headless browser run and twelve corrected edge probes, not statistical availability measurements.
Raw NetLog, endpoint secret path, challenge URLs, tokens and local routing details remain private. No system settings or production rules changed.
